main_body: Tall brick townhouse: a slate mansard roof with a flat top and a dormer, an orange cornice, then three brick storeys with stone-framed windows, a balcony and a green door.
top_band: Rows 17-23 at x=24: a lighter grey-blue roof-top plate (L=95, edged by L=122 lines at rows 17 and 23). Below it, a darker slate slope begins at row 24.
evidence: The column scan shows a light roof-top band (rows 17-23), a 1-row lighter edge line at row 23, and a dark shadow row (L=53) at row 24. Below that come the slate slope (rows 25-43), the orange cornice (rows 44-46) and the brick facade. The roof surface is visibly seen from above, and the windows have stone surrounds with inset glass. The top band is thin compared with the building height, but it reads as a roof surface with a front edge and shadow. No receding side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The brick and slate have several tones, and the brick has per-course variation. The measured facts are 14 colours per tile and 2% flat fill, which is in line with the references. The weak points are the outline and the palette depth. 90% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the piece has a near-black sticker outline instead of dark material-tone edges. It also has only 49 distinct colours, against 185 and 66 for the references, so the ramps are thinner than Beodeul's. Because of the neutral outline, it does not match the Beodeul standard.
